hot.title: Stabilizing On-Policy Targeted Guidance in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
hot.summary: The authors introduce targeted guidance for multi-turn software-engineering reinforcement learning, placing textual feedback before a failing turn and distilling the same model’s hint-conditioned token predictions only there, alongside ordinary rewards. In their coding setup, Markdown reward is 0.85 ± 0.09 versus 0.00 ± 0.00 for GRPO, while coding pass-rate is 0.33 ± 0.05 versus 0.33 ± 0.07; findings are limited to this setting and designed feedback.

hot.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
hot.summary: FrontierPhysics evaluates whether AI agents can conduct open-ended physics research from high-level briefs. The benchmark uses physicist-contributed research tasks and grades structured outputs with deterministic checks, alongside manuscripts and research trajectories against expert-authored rubrics. Passing requires all verifier tests and blocking criteria. The top tested configuration passed 46/168 trials (27.4%), measuring performance under this protocol rather than human publication acceptance.

hot.title: From Pixels to Actions - Towards Native Vision-Language-Action Policies
hot.summary: NEO-VLA combines image patches and language in one backbone and lets an action expert read selected layers to generate continuous action chunks. In frozen-backbone LIBERO evaluation, it reaches 90.9% average success, versus 79.5% for Qwen3-VL 2B. The comparison does not isolate encoder removal as the cause, and performance under object-position perturbations falls to 3.0%.

hot.title: Together Compiler: Continual Compilation for AI Inference
hot.summary: TKCC enables agents to optimize inference deployments as workloads change by hot-reloading candidate forward passes in a persistent engine, screening them before representative measurements. Its cost model selects GPU-parallelism configurations. On B200 GLM 5.3, two-tier measurement evaluated 1,354 candidates versus 168 for a single slow tier and found a 7.2% faster solution; the result is specific to that comparison.

hot.title: You don't need long context
hot.summary: The authors test whether agents need full histories or documents in active context using compact handoff states and tool-based retrieval. In long-horizon and long-input tasks these approaches preserve or improve results. For Qwen 3 Coder Next, a 16K rather than 256K context window yielded 7× more decoded tokens per second; this measures throughput, not task time, and evidence is limited.

hot.title: VABAR: A Variational Automation Benchmark for Agentic Robotics
hot.summary: VABAR evaluates agentic robot programs across six simulated tasks with structured, physically feasible variations. It uses reusable perception, planning, and control skills, and records success and diagnostics. On Gear Meshing Level 1, autonomously generated GaP succeeds on 70.0% of instances, versus 0.0% for Claude Code and 100.0% for a human-authored graph; these results are simulated, not evidence of real-world operation.

hot.title: GSBR: Geometric Support Behavior Regularization for Online RL
hot.summary: GSBR guides online robot learning by penalizing actions only outside neighborhoods around sampled actions from a pretrained controller. This lets the actor choose among supported behaviors while permitting nearby improvements at a distance-based cost. Across 19 tasks in four benchmarks, GSBR averages 95% success and 0.95 normalized throughput, versus RLT’s 0.77; on LIBERO, RLT has higher success.

hot.title: VFlash: Fast, Accurate Visual Planning via Flash Primitive Decoding
hot.summary: VFlash generates spatial plans for vision-language models by drafting complete structured primitives, such as trajectories, in parallel, while retaining target-verified decoding for text. On MolmoSpaces, a world action model using VFlash plans reaches 70.2% success versus 61.0% with autoregressive plans. On Jetson Thor, batch-one model-pipeline latency is 703.3 ms versus 3,552.7 ms; this is not full robot response time.

hot.title: CompressionBench: How can your coding agents compress LLMs?
hot.summary: The authors introduce CompressionBench, where coding agents design compressed models and inference code under storage limits, then undergo independent verification. Across six tasks, 29 of 36 submissions passed. Selecting the lowest-perplexity design per task yielded a 3.4% mean perplexity increase over BF16 and 77.33% downstream accuracy, versus 79.56% for BF16; results show storage fit, not faster decoding or measured energy savings.

hot.title: Reinforcement Learning Enables Scaling Generalist Robot Policy Improvement
hot.summary: The authors evaluate critic-guided reinforcement learning for improving a generalist robot policy across simulated manipulation tasks. The methods learn from experience across varied tasks and use action-value estimates to guide action selection or policy updates. In MolmoSpaces, gains reach 58 percentage points on unseen scenes and 39 on unseen objects, but are maxima in tested settings, not arbitrary-task generalization.

hot.title: On the Volume Conjectures for Dehn-Filled 3-Manifolds Along Fundamental Shadow Link Complements With Big Volume
hot.summary: The authors prove large-level asymptotics for Reshetikhin–Turaev invariants of hyperbolic 3-manifolds obtained by integral Dehn filling fundamental shadow link complements. They extend quantum 6j symbols and use approximate reflection symmetry to cancel problematic Fourier coefficients while preserving asymptotics. Both conjectures hold at positive odd levels when manifold volume is sufficiently close to the starting complement’s; this does not cover all fillings.

hot.title: Perceptive Humanoid Motion from Simulation
hot.summary: HALO trains a humanoid robot to turn language requests and camera views into whole-body actions. It uses simulated homes to generate paired vision-language-motion examples while people still author task prompts and motion keyframes. In six unseen, unmapped real-world homes, it achieves 91% mean success across six tested single-task skills, not longer sequences. Its stack combines planning, generation, and tracking.

hot.title: Open-HumanWAM: An Open Recipe for Scaling Human and Robot Experience for Embodied Foundation Models
hot.summary: Open-HumanWAM studies whether curated first-person human videos can improve robot manipulation. It aligns hand motion and language across video sources into a shared action representation, then tests robot post-training and hybrid, goal-conditioned control. In simulation, scene-OOD success rises from 49.1% at 100 hours to 73.2% at 50,000 hours with IDM; this empirical result covers tested settings only.

hot.title: BabyTheorist: A Benchmark for Learning to Theorize the World from Observation Alone
hot.summary: BabyTheorist tests whether learners acquire reusable rules from ungrouped visual examples and apply them to new cases. It trains on unlabeled before-and-after grids generated by hidden programs, then evaluates transfer across a curriculum. Seven representative baselines stop within the first two of eight levels; NEO reaches Level 2 in Single modes but fails Level 1 in Multi modes.

hot.title: Interactive World Simulation with Cosmos for Physical AI
hot.summary: The authors adapt pretrained Cosmos 3 into three control-conditioned visual simulators using causal chunks, bounded history, and a four-stage training recipe. The systems predict observations from robot, scene, or driving controls, with an external simulator maintaining physical state in one mode. In a matched 30-case comparison, the final SF-DMD stage improves quality and reference agreement, but its isolated cause and general closed-loop utility remain unestablished.

hot.title: Turns Matter: Advancing Streaming Video RL via Turn-Level Credit
hot.summary: TurnWise trains streaming video assistants to decide whether to respond or wait by assigning group-relative advantages to each decision from remaining returns after later actions are replaced with silence, and averaging loss across turns. On Qwen2.5-VL-3B, it scores 43.56 PAUC on ProactiveVQA, 21.59 Timing F1 on OVO-Timing, and 49.43 accuracy on StreamingBench, leading non-TurnWise results on these benchmarks.

hot.title: SinkState: On-the-Fly SVD of Recurrent States for Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving
hot.summary: SINKSTATE reduces recurrent-state traffic during linear-attention decoding by maintaining an adaptive low-rank representation. It buffers token updates, applies local SVD updates, and asynchronously consolidates frozen components on the CPU. In evaluation on four Mamba-2/GDN models, Nemotron-3-Nano-4B achieved 1.58× speedup on MATH-500, while peak recurrent-state memory averaged 0.52 of dense baselines and benchmark accuracy changed without a consistent loss.

hot.title: ServerBench: How can your coding agents design specialized LLM serving systems?
hot.summary: ServerBench evaluates coding agents on building a complete language-model serving system for a fixed model, GPU allocation, and coding workload, while choosing session concurrency. It replays dependent sessions and scores completed requests meeting both time-to-first-token and per-output-token latency targets, per GPU cost. Claude Sonnet 5.5 reaches 2.97 dollars per dollar on Gemma E4B versus vLLM’s 0.61, within the evaluated deployment.

hot.title: Adversarial Speculative Reasoning Improves Long Horizon Agents
hot.summary: The authors use speculative decoding to steer selected decisions into less noisy context positions. A trained draft is more likely to be rejected at those points, so the target resamples at the start of a fresh verification block while preserving its token distribution. On DeepSWE, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 pass rate rises from 60.6% to 67.6%; not all benchmark gains are statistically established.

hot.title: Non-Unitary Quantum Butterfly Effect: Theory and Experiment
hot.summary: The authors track local perturbations with circuit echoes and an out-of-time-order correlator (OTOC), analyzing Haar-random brickwork circuits with measurements modeled as dephasing. Measurements leave a causal front visible but attenuate the signal inside it; sparse-measurement theory predicts a decay timescale proportional to p^(-1/2) in the thermodynamic Gaussian regime. An eight-qubit trapped-ion demonstration resolves structure, but does not validate the prediction.

likes.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
likes.summary: The authors show that GPT-6 Astra, a general-purpose frontier LLM, can read and write neural network weights directly, without gradient descent or trained helper models. Across eight experiments it identifies what small networks were trained on from their weights, fixes and writes game-playing policies, and edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to stop reasoning loops. They call this Weight-Space Programming.

likes.title: Mistral Large 4
likes.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model whose authors examine long-context attention for agentic coding. They find architecture variants with similar language-modeling loss can differ on SWE-bench Verified, while knowledge-based evaluations show no analogous gap. The final system restores long-context access in more layers and uses DSA to select past tokens; its benchmark results do not isolate DSA’s effect.

likes.title: Meta$^2$: Precomputing Reusable Knowledge for Online Harness Evolution in Long-Horizon Agents
likes.summary: Meta² teaches an evolver reusable guidance for changing a frozen model’s task harness during a run, rather than selecting one harness for every task. Its Meta-Skill guides when to edit, hold, or avoid changes; edits remain run-local, without held-out verifier feedback. With GPT-5.6-Terra, it reports mean@5 81.00% on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and mean@3 44.44% on DeepSWE 1.1, on two tested benchmarks.

likes.title: Hierarchical World Models with Implicit Dynamics
likes.summary: ID-WM separates choosing intermediate states from choosing actions to make long-horizon planning in world models manageable. A diffusion model proposes nearby subgoals, and an action-conditioned model searches for actions to reach them, with planning repeated locally. In state-based PushT random-goal trials, it succeeds in 77% versus 21% for single-level world-model MPC; this result is limited to the tested benchmark setting.

likes.title: Hinted Scaling Laws
likes.summary: The authors develop benchmark hinting to forecast downstream accuracy when smaller models score near zero. They add graded solution help, fit its relationship with model scale, and predict the unhinted score. On Delphi, logit mixing predicted 25.9% GSM8K accuracy for a 10^23-FLOP model within 3 percentage points, using models trained with at most 10^20 FLOPs. This result uses a solution-prompted teacher.

likes.title: On the Generalization Limitation of On-Policy Distillation for Post-RL Consolidation
likes.summary: The authors test whether on-policy distillation transfers specialist improvements beyond supervised tasks. A student learns from its own responses with teacher guidance; multi-teacher training routes domains to matching teachers. Narrow math supervision nearly matches teacher scores in-distribution but leaves out-of-distribution performance 3.73% below base. Broader data with a stronger teacher raises scores across five benchmarks, but effects are not isolated.

likes.title: Automating AI R&D for Molecular Discovery
likes.summary: Intology evaluates Locus, its autonomous AI R&D system, on three molecular discovery tasks: proprietary molecular property prediction, adapting Boltz-2 for small-molecule potency prediction, and designing antibody workflows around BoltzGen/Boltz-2 and ESMC/ESMFold2. Under matched compute, Locus outperforms Claude Code, Codex, and baselines from Boltz and BioHub, generalizing better from limited data and finding more sample-efficient solutions.

likes.title: Latent Sparse Attention: Towards Subquadratic Ultra-Long Context Attention
likes.summary: The authors introduce Latent Sparse Attention (LSA), which groups similar keys and searches group representatives before retrieving selected original keys for attention. Its Flat variant scans all group centroids, while Tree uses hierarchical search. On GLM-5.3-FLASH, Flat makes one layer’s prefill 22.7× faster at 10M tokens than the model’s sparse-attention baseline; this is not an end-to-end speedup.

likes.title: IdeaTaste: Do LLMs Share the Research Taste of Human Researchers?
likes.summary: IdeaTaste tests whether AI research agents make choices resembling those of human communities. It generates proposals from literature frozen at the end of 2025, then compares their citations and ideas with papers published in January–August 2026. Agents reach about 26% of human level on citation matching and 18% on idea matching, but publication similarity measures community choices, not objective research quality.

likes.title: Democratizing Robot-Use Agents: A Unified Harness with Open Models
likes.summary: The authors introduce uni-robot-agent, a shared robot-interaction harness that lets adapters translate common tools and execution feedback across models and environments. On RoboDojo, open-weight Qwen3.8-Flash-Next scores 31.39 without privileged simulator inputs, above the published GPT-6 Astra–RoboProbe score of 28.97; this is not a matched comparison, since evaluations used 252 and 2,100 episodes, respectively.

likes.title: CoworkOS:Scaling Agent Coworkers for Real-world Automation
likes.summary: CoworkOS addresses complex work by letting a Main Agent direct delegated tasks while a Coordinator tracks assignments and feedback, and Subagents execute bounded work. Persistent jobs, memory, and shared resources support continuity across interruptions. In a five-round post-training case study, the mean across eight benchmark scores rose from 33.19 to 42.95; this measured increase does not isolate CoworkOS’s causal effect.

likes.title: Introducing Ripple-65B Preview, a Frontier Open-Weight Model
likes.summary: Ricursive Intelligence releases Ripple-65B Preview, a general-purpose variant of the proprietary language model that powers its AI chip design platform. The dense 65B model was trained from scratch on 12 trillion tokens with up to 1M context, and reaches 80.52 on TerminalBench 2.1, a new U.S. open-weight state of the art for agentic coding. The full R&D cost was $32M, which the team estimates is one-tenth that of the previous open-weight SOTA.

likes.title: Statistical Foundations of Reinforcement Learning: A Non-Asymptotic Perspective
likes.summary: The monograph synthesizes finite-sample guarantees for tabular reinforcement learning across generative-model, online, and offline data settings, comparing algorithmic upper bounds with minimax lower bounds. It explains how sampling conditions shape effective methods and uncertainty strategies. Online, MVP achieves high-probability regret O(min{√(SAH³K), HK}) for every K ≥ 1, matching the minimax lower bound up to logarithmic factors in finite-horizon nonstationary MDPs.

likes.title: Hierarchical Residuals: A Minimalist Decoupling of Residual Width from Compute Width
likes.summary: HiRes separates carried residual width from layer-computation width in Transformers. It carries a wider state between groups of ordinary PreNorm layers, which still compute at width d, using block-boundary projections and RMSNorm. In five model-size comparisons, its fitted training FLOPs to validation loss 3.00 are lower; the vanilla baseline requires 1.30× as much, but this is not a wall-clock speedup.
